actions.Finding headline: Check the applicable scheme, not a general industry label
actions.Why it matters: An unsupported coverage assumption can leave registration, returns or contributions unresolved.
actions.Practical first step: Check each work location and covered activity with the relevant scheme authority. Record the coverage decision and any registration or reporting actions.
actions.Evidence of completion: A jurisdiction-specific coverage record and evidence of required registration, returns and contributions.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: Changed activities, locations, scheme rules or covered workers.
actions.Small-business application: A dated role/pay register, a short sample check and an owner for exceptions can be sufficient evidence of the process.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Sample different roles, instruments, pay patterns and locations. Record exception escalation and independent review responsibilities.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Targeted payroll, award/classification or salary-arrangement review, scoped to the flagged population.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Obtain a supported industry and jurisdiction coverage decision and identify applicable scheme tasks.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Reconcile required registrations, returns and contributions with workforce data, while maintaining ordinary leave obligations where applicable.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Assuming a portable scheme replaces every ordinary long-service-leave obligation.
actions.Recheck trigger: Changed activities, locations, scheme rules or covered workers.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B12_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Confirm the flexibility arrangement is the right legal mechanism
actions.Why it matters: Consent alone may not satisfy an IFA's permitted scope, documentation and better-off-overall requirements.
actions.Practical first step: Identify what each IFA varies and review its basis and effect against the relevant instrument. Keep the employee's genuine agreement and comparison on file.
actions.Evidence of completion: A reviewed IFA, comparison and record of agreement, with a review trigger.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: New IFAs or changed pay, hours, circumstances or instrument terms.
actions.Small-business application: A current terms register and a controlled set of suitable templates can be proportionate.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Use controlled templates, approval limits and version/variation tracking across entities and roles.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Employment terms and engagement review, with legal referral for issues outside the agreed HR advisory scope.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Check the specific terms being varied and the employee's position under the applicable instrument.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Retain the supported comparison and required agreement, and review when relevant circumstances change.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Calling any flexible roster or work-from-home agreement an IFA.
actions.Recheck trigger: New IFAs or changed pay, hours, circumstances or instrument terms.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B13_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Keep required credentials current
actions.Why it matters: Expired or inappropriate credentials may permit work that should not proceed without a current authorisation.
actions.Practical first step: List the credentials required by each relevant role, verify current evidence and set an escalation before expiry or restriction.
actions.Evidence of completion: A current credential register and clear controls preventing unauthorised work.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: Before relevant work and on expiry, restriction or suspension.
actions.Small-business application: A short pre-start and first-week checklist with named follow-up can work well.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Coordinate manager, payroll, IT and site responsibilities; sample completion and starter understanding.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Practical onboarding workflow and required-information controls.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Verify relevant credentials and task restrictions, assign monitoring responsibility and define what happens on expiry or suspension.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Test one upcoming expiry and confirm work allocation prevents an unauthorised task.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Treating a reminder email as sufficient without checking the response to expiry.
actions.Recheck trigger: Before relevant work and on expiry, restriction or suspension.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B14_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Keep responsibility for technology-assisted people decisions
actions.Why it matters: Unchecked outputs can affect applicants or employees without an adequate basis, appropriate data handling or a meaningful review route.
actions.Practical first step: List the tools, decisions and personal information involved. Review human oversight, provider access and applicable privacy-policy disclosures before the relevant deadline.
actions.Evidence of completion: The people-technology review is complete, relevant data and decision safeguards are implemented, and accountable humans can explain and review affected decisions. Applicable transparency duties have been met by their actual due date; future requirements stay on the dated plan.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: A new tool, changed use, material error or applicable law change.
actions.Small-business application: A secure, organised repository with controlled access and tested recovery can be sufficient; a particular HR system is not required.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Review role-based access, supplier arrangements, retention, logs and recovery across the employee lifecycle.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Employment-record process review and coordination with privacy/cyber specialists where necessary.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Record the tool, purpose, data and decisions affected. Test meaningful human review, relevant bias and applicable transparency requirements.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Review a sample decision and test whether an error can be challenged and corrected without relying on the same output again.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Treating a human clicking approve as evidence of meaningful oversight.
actions.Recheck trigger: A new tool, changed use, material error or applicable law change.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B15_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Extend safety checks beyond the main workplace
actions.Why it matters: Reliance on the worker or another site can leave foreseeable isolation, travel, aggression or communication risks unmanaged.
actions.Practical first step: Review one representative remote, isolated or client-site arrangement with the worker and any other duty holder. Confirm risks, contacts and controls.
actions.Evidence of completion: A documented work-setting review and tested communication/escalation arrangement.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: New work settings, host arrangements or a failed contact procedure.
actions.Small-business application: Keep a usable risk/control record and test emergency and injury contacts for the actual work.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Test different tasks, locations and duty-holder interfaces; use competent specialist input where needed.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: HR/return-to-work coordination and referral to a competent WHS or insurance specialist where needed.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Agree site-specific controls, responsibilities and communication with relevant workers and other duty holders.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Test the check-in or emergency arrangement and reassess tasks or settings not yet covered.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Assuming the host workplace automatically manages every duty for the employer.
actions.Recheck trigger: New work settings, host arrangements or a failed contact procedure.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B16_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Check the reporting scope at organisation and group level
actions.Why it matters: An incorrect group or eligibility assumption can leave a reporting obligation without a responsible owner.
actions.Practical first step: Confirm eligibility, past reporting status and relevant group structure with current WGEA guidance. Allocate reporting responsibilities and key dates.
actions.Evidence of completion: An eligibility and reporting-scope record, with evidence of any required lodgement and follow-up.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: Changed headcount, corporate structure, reporting history or reporting rules.
actions.Small-business application: Use direct conversations with a safe alternative for sensitive issues. Do not promise anonymity where individuals can be inferred.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Combine employee listening with manager/site patterns and visible follow-through; protect confidentiality in small subgroups.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Employee listening, retention diagnosis and accountable leadership practices.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Confirm the organisation and group scope using the relevant reporting rules and history.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Allocate required submissions and follow-up actions and retain evidence of completion.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Using the Fair Work small-business count as the reporting eligibility test.
actions.Recheck trigger: Changed headcount, corporate structure, reporting history or reporting rules.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B17_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Test the redundancy process, not only the payment
actions.Why it matters: A payment calculation does not establish a genuine redundancy or a sound selection, consultation and redeployment process.
actions.Practical first step: Obtain a pre-decision review of the proposed structure, rationale, consultation and redeployment steps, and applicable payments.
actions.Evidence of completion: A supported redundancy plan and decision record prepared at the appropriate stage of the process.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: Any proposed role removal or material restructure.
actions.Small-business application: A short pre-decision and departure checklist with advice for a live high-risk matter can be proportionate.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Separate decision approval, payroll checking, system access and handover ownership; test that the handovers work.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Pre-decision HR review, final-pay coordination and legal referral where the matter requires it.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Document the operational proposal and check the relevant consultation, selection, redeployment and entitlement requirements.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Review the decision trail and unresolved alternatives before communicating an employment-ending decision.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Using redundancy as a substitute for addressing a performance or conduct concern.
actions.Recheck trigger: Any proposed role removal or material restructure.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B18_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Test consistency where decisions are made
actions.Why it matters: A centrally issued policy may produce different decisions if managers interpret or apply it differently.
actions.Practical first step: Compare recent decisions on one issue, such as probation or flexible work, across managers. Identify unexplained differences and provide targeted guidance.
actions.Evidence of completion: A sample of comparable people decisions shows that the agreed criteria are used consistently, relevant differences are explained and identified errors or unfair inconsistencies have been addressed and checked.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: New managers, a material policy change or repeated inconsistency.
actions.Small-business application: Regular recorded check-ins can provide a sound process without a complex annual appraisal system.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Check consistency between managers and whether evidence, support and review decisions meet agreed standards.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Manager coaching and a fair performance or conduct process for the identified situation.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Compare a small sample of like decisions and distinguish justified differences from avoidable inconsistency.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Give targeted guidance and recheck later decisions in the affected teams.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Assuming equal outcomes are always required despite different facts, or ignoring unexplained variation.
actions.Recheck trigger: New managers, a material policy change or repeated inconsistency.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B19_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Make after-hours expectations explicit
actions.Why it matters: Unclear availability expectations can create disputes about contact, rest, personal circumstances and payment.
actions.Practical first step: Agree which situations genuinely require contact, who is available and how availability is recognised. Check the arrangement against applicable rights and pay rules.
actions.Evidence of completion: Out-of-hours expectations and any work/payment arrangements are clear. The business has tested how it will assess a refusal to monitor, read or respond unless that refusal is unreasonable, and has addressed any current concern using the relevant circumstances.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: Changed contact expectations, duties or an after-hours dispute.
actions.Small-business application: Use concise policies addressing actual work; do not create a large handbook merely to improve the score.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Control versions and confirm managers apply the same expectations and request processes across teams.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Proportionate policy review and manager implementation support.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Discuss necessary contact, the relevant circumstances, any on-call or payment arrangement and how refusal will be assessed.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Check what happens in practice and correct pressure to remain available beyond the agreed and lawful arrangement.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Treating the right as a total contact ban, or assuming a managerial title removes it.
actions.Recheck trigger: Changed contact expectations, duties or an after-hours dispute.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B20_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Use the actual agreement, not a generic award checklist
actions.Why it matters: Maintaining headline rates alone can miss agreement rules governing classifications, allowances and employment decisions.
actions.Practical first step: Map the applicable agreement and coverage to affected roles, then check key payroll and employment processes against its current operation.
actions.Evidence of completion: Applicable agreement obligations are mapped to actual processes, identified differences have been corrected and the affected pay, hours or decision process has been checked again.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: Agreement variation, replacement, termination or an operational change.
actions.Small-business application: A dated role/pay register, a short sample check and an owner for exceptions can be sufficient evidence of the process.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Sample different roles, instruments, pay patterns and locations. Record exception escalation and independent review responsibilities.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Targeted payroll, award/classification or salary-arrangement review, scoped to the flagged population.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Map the applicable agreement and current obligations to payroll and relevant people processes.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Check a changed rate and an exception scenario, including how updates reach each responsible person.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Assuming nominal expiry automatically ends the agreement.
actions.Recheck trigger: Agreement variation, replacement, termination or an operational change.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B21_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Build consultation into the change plan
actions.Why it matters: Late consultation can prevent genuine consideration of employee views and leave required process steps uncompleted.
actions.Practical first step: For the next material change, identify affected workers and representatives, required information and consultation timing before implementation commitments are made.
actions.Evidence of completion: Required information and consultation occurred at the appropriate stage, employee views were genuinely considered, the outcome was communicated and resulting commitments were implemented and checked. Obtain any separately required agreement.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: A material change to work, rosters, technology or structure.
actions.Small-business application: Use concise policies addressing actual work; do not create a large handbook merely to improve the score.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Control versions and confirm managers apply the same expectations and request processes across teams.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Proportionate policy review and manager implementation support.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Identify the applicable trigger, timing and affected employees or representatives, then provide the necessary information and opportunity for input.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Record how views were considered before the relevant step is finalised, and check any separate consent requirements.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Calling a finished-decision announcement consultation, or assuming consultation always means negotiation.
actions.Recheck trigger: A material change to work, rosters, technology or structure.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B22_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Keep special-rate eligibility and progression current
actions.Why it matters: A reduced or starting rate may cease to be appropriate when age, duties, competency or training conditions change.
actions.Practical first step: Check each affected employee's training arrangement, duties and progression dates against current requirements and payroll settings.
actions.Evidence of completion: An eligibility and progression register with current evidence and payroll updates.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: An age, competency, duties or training milestone.
actions.Small-business application: A dated role/pay register, a short sample check and an owner for exceptions can be sufficient evidence of the process.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Sample different roles, instruments, pay patterns and locations. Record exception escalation and independent review responsibilities.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: Targeted payroll, award/classification or salary-arrangement review, scoped to the flagged population.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Verify the applicable basis and progression triggers for each affected arrangement.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Test a recent milestone and set responsibility for future changes in payroll and records.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Using a lower rate solely because someone is young or learning a role.
actions.Recheck trigger: An age, competency, duties or training milestone.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B23_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Resolve the shortfall and prevent its recurrence
actions.Why it matters: Fixing only the next payment can leave earlier entitlements unpaid or the same error affecting other people.
actions.Practical first step: Preserve the relevant pay and work records, allocate an owner and confirm what has been reported before deciding the scope of review.
actions.Evidence of completion: A documented scope and calculation, correction and communication record, related obligation checks and a successful follow-up payroll test.
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: Any suspected or identified shortfall and completion of its correction.
actions.Small-business application: Use a concise record with a named owner and a practical check. The outcome matters more than the size of the document.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Check each materially different work arrangement, team or location and specify handovers and escalation.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: A targeted review of the flagged issue, practical implementation support and specialist referral where necessary.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Establish the affected rule, period and population; calculate the correction and related obligations and communicate appropriately.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Complete and record the correction, repair the cause and test a later affected pay cycle.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Treating a changed payroll setting as evidence that past underpayments have been resolved.
actions.Recheck trigger: Any suspected or identified shortfall and completion of its correction.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B24_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Remove the work barrier through a considered adjustment
actions.Why it matters: A standard process may disadvantage a person where a workplace adjustment should be considered before a decision or task proceeds.
actions.Practical first step: Arrange a private discussion about the work-related barrier and the outcome needed. Seek only information relevant to assessing the adjustment.
actions.Evidence of completion: A proportionate record of the barrier, options considered, decision and implementation, with a review of effectiveness and restricted information access.
actions.Suggested owner: Owner / HR lead with the employee
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: An adjustment request, identified barrier or changed requirements.
actions.Small-business application: Use a concise record with a named owner and a practical check. The outcome matters more than the size of the document.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Check each materially different work arrangement, team or location and specify handovers and escalation.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: A targeted review of the flagged issue, practical implementation support and specialist referral where necessary.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Discuss the work-related barrier, essential job requirements and practical adjustment options with the person, seeking relevant advice where needed.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Record the decision and reasoning, implement agreed measures and review whether the barrier has been addressed.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Seeking more medical detail than needed or assuming an adjustment is impossible without considering options.
actions.Recheck trigger: An adjustment request, identified barrier or changed requirements.

actions.Priority / trigger: Use B25_0 / _1 / _2 / _3 / _DK in Answer Outcomes, then apply Risk Context. Weight is not the risk rating.
actions.Finding headline: Close the gaps between organisations sharing the work
actions.Why it matters: A worker can fall between organisations when each assumes the other manages induction, supervision, hazards or incident response.
actions.Practical first step: List the shared tasks and responsible organisations, then check with the worker where induction, supervision or reporting responsibilities are unclear.
actions.Evidence of completion: An agreed responsibility record, worker induction and consultation evidence, task-specific controls and a tested incident handover.
actions.Suggested owner: Operational lead with the other duty holder
actions.Suggested timing: Risk Method timing is the initial response target; actual duties and earlier events take precedence. Recheck: A new placement, changed task, site or shared-work arrangement.
actions.Small-business application: Use a concise record with a named owner and a practical check. The outcome matters more than the size of the document.
actions.Larger / more complex application: Check each materially different work arrangement, team or location and specify handovers and escalation.
actions.Optional DreamStoneHR support: A targeted review of the flagged issue, practical implementation support and specialist referral where necessary.
actions.Step 2: establish or repair: Agree who performs each safety task with the other duty holder and the worker, without treating the arrangement as a transfer of legal duties.
actions.Step 3: test effectiveness: Check the induction, actual task allocation, controls and incident handover before relying on the arrangement.
actions.Avoid this shortcut: Assuming the labour-hire provider or host carries every duty because of the contract.
actions.Recheck trigger: A new placement, changed task, site or shared-work arrangement.
